title: Denver dumps Flock, awards location tracking camera contract to Axon
summary: Denver is ending its ALPR contract with Flock Safety and awarding a new contract to Axon, pending council approval. The decision follows 9NEWS investigations revealing Flock shared Denver data with federal immigration enforcement and a city auditor's refusal to countersign the Flock contract.

key_quotes.quote: Denver is getting rid of its controversial automated license plate reading (ALPR) camera vendor Flock Safety, choosing to award its new ALPR contract to Axon

the company placed Denver's tracking data on a national network accessible to law enforcement agencies that assisted immigration enforcement, and after 9NEWS uncovered the company had a secret partnership with the U.S. Border Patrol
Denver City Auditor Tim O'Brien announced last Friday that he could not, in good conscience, countersign the city's contract with Flock
